entries.71f699b4b0e58329: Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥2,663 million, down 7.6% from ¥2,882 million in the previous fiscal year. Revenue was ¥2,001 million for the PIXTA business, ¥502 million for the fotowa business and ¥159 million for other businesses. The decrease in the PIXTA business was a reaction to revenue recorded in the previous fiscal year from a large-scale project.

entries.81b4daf3ca47fcff: Under its corporate philosophy of “Connecting talent, making the world positive,” while its main business is operating an online marketplace covering everything from sourcing to selling digital materials, it aims to realize a “creative platform economy” composed of numerous creative platforms. As its medium-term business policy, the company aims to become a “visual platform” that leverages synergies among businesses to comprehensively address various visual needs of corporations and individuals, and states that it will advance investment aimed at regaining revenue growth while maintaining a certain profit level for the next 3 years or so.
entries.85ab929104f04820: This is a reportable segment that operates fotowa (Fotowa), an on-site photography platform for family and children's portraits. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥502 million. For newborn photography, Shichi-Go-San and other children's milestones and events, users can book a preferred photographer by specifying time and location and have family commemorative photos taken. Following a change in the terms of use in December 2024, the contract form changed from a matching service (intermediary contract) to a self-provided service (contracting), and revenue recognition changed from net to gross.

entries.cd6dccaea77ab478: This is a reportable segment that operates PIXTA, an online marketplace for digital content such as photos, illustrations, videos, and music. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥2,001 million. Materials are collected from creators in Japan and abroad in a crowdsourcing format, and all are sold to corporations and individuals under royalty-free licenses. When materials are sold, creators are granted acquired credits according to the sales price and commission rate.
